title: The Sharing Gap - All Things Product Podcast with Teresa Torres & Petra Wille
text: The Sharing Gap - All Things Product Podcast with Teresa Torres & Petra Wille Our Courses Train Your Team Articles Just Now Possible Get in Touch Sign in Subscribe The Sharing Gap - All Things Product Podcast with Teresa Torres & Petra Wille Teresa Torres 17 Nov 2026 14 min Listen to this episode on: Spotify | Apple Podcasts Why has everyone stopped sharing their real product work — and what do we lose when the field goes quiet? Petra Wille and Teresa Torres return to the never-ending social-media question, this time from a trend angle: the genuinely useful stories — the how, the messy middle, the small wins — are drying up, replaced by platitudes and AI slop. Petra, who coaches product leaders daily, keeps seeing brilliant work in private that no one is willing to post, held back by the fear that everyone else is further ahead. Teresa shares why she overhauled her own strategy two years ago — writing only about what she’s personally doing (Claude Code, a year of building AI evals) — and why every piece has performed better since. The payoff is a practical, low-stakes challenge for anyone who feels behind or unsure what they’re even allowed to share: a simple way to start building the muscle. The guiding idea — write for the person one step behind you. Key Takeaways The useful stuff — the how, the practice, the messy learnings — is disappearing from social media, crowded out by platitudes and AI slop. Leaders are sitting on great work but won’t share it, convinced everyone else is further ahead and their own story is “too small” or “too niche.” Even an “unglamorous” result is valuable — e.g., “we tried 20 things, it was different work but no efficiency gains” is a learning others need. It’s imposter syndrome at the product level: like every team certain a competitor does it better, we’re too close to our own work to see what’s interesting. Teresa’s fix: stop writing generic guides and share only what you’re personally doing — specificity and a real point of view are what differentiate you now. Personal, specific stories consistently outperform platitudes — humans react to lived experience, not AI slop. Try the 5-day challenge: each day, pick the most interesting thing that happened and post it. Most posts get ignored (so it’s low-risk), and you build the habit. No matter where you are, someone’s a step behind you — write for them. Describe what you faced, what you did, and what you hope happens; you don’t need the ending. Notable Moments “We need to get into the how — what are you putting into practice? That’s the stuff that’s valuable to share.” — Teresa “I would encourage people to share more — even if it’s unfinished, even if it’s small — and not just leave the field to the thought leaders.” — Petra “I made a very deliberate decision: I’m only going to write about things that I am personally doing.” — Teresa “When we write platitudes and AI slop, humans don’t react to it. Share your personal experience — that’s what we want to read.” — Teresa “There’s always going to be someone a step ahead of you. But there’s also always someone a step behind you.
